prize_parts.citation: for establishing nominal rigidities as the basis of modern monetary policy analysis, through time-dependent and staggered price and wage setting, interest-rate policy rules, and a micro-founded, welfare-based theory of monetary policy

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B014, credited to Calvo, Taylor and Woodford. I judge it on the criterion I stated in round 1, a specific scientific contribution with large and durable consequences. Three separable contributions carry the framework. Calvo supplied the tractable pricing friction. Taylor supplied staggered contracts and a policy rule that could be estimated and communicated. Woodford integrated them into a micro-founded theory of interest and prices with an explicit welfare criterion. The framework has been tested against the 2008 crisis, the zero lower bound and the 2021-23 inflation. In each case it was revised and extended, and it remains the baseline against which heterogeneous-agent work is defined, including by its critics. No earlier prize recognised the pricing-friction and policy-rule core, as opposed to rational expectations, time consistency, identification methods or banking crises. I reworded the citation after the exchange so that it credits the primitives and the synthesis. It does not claim the estimated-DSGE tradition, and it does not rank the omitted contributors below the three named. I weigh prior prizes by whether the specific contribution was already recognised, not by topic proximity, and I apply that standard equally to B014 and to B003 (2022), B032 (2024) and B047 (2008). My alternatives now are B003 and B047. B003 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and its supporters have credibly separated it from the 2022 prize. B047 is mature and has stable two-name attribution. Neither displaces B014 for me on breadth of influence on practice and on research.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the main weakness. Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Gertler, Smets and Wouters have serious claims, and the three-person cap excludes people whose work made the framework estimable and usable in central banks. No citation wording removes that cost, and the committee should accept it openly. Calvo's contribution is a compact device, and a reasonable member could ask whether it is a discovery of the kind the committee normally rewards. I think it is, because the Phillips curve and the policy analysis built on it rest on it, but that is a judgement call. Representative-agent versions are widely seen as superseded, and a prize could be read as rewarding a stage of development, not an end state. The post-2021 inflation is an unresolved test of maturity, and I do not claim to have settled it. B003 has the tidier attribution. My reservations about it are its thin direct empirical identification in the original paper and the proximity of the 2022 prize. I have not verified priority or attribution claims beyond my own knowledge of the literature.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers B003 for its single mechanism and two originators. He says he would support B014 if the committee found a defensible narrower citation or attribution, and that the citation must say whether it rewards the pricing friction, the policy rule or the integrated framework.
responses.response: I take that condition as the right test and have tried to meet it. The revised citation names three components and ties them to three people: pricing friction (Calvo), contracts and rule (Taylor), and the micro-founded welfare-based synthesis (Woodford). These are the primitives on which the estimated models were built. It does not purport to credit the estimation tradition. I cannot make the attribution as clean as Kiyotaki-Moore, and I do not claim to. I also accept your point that collateral-driven amplification is a different discovery from the work recognised in 2022, so I do not rely on the prior-prize argument against B003. My ordering rests on breadth of influence on both research and policy practice, and on the fact that B003's original contribution is theoretical with identification coming mainly from later work. If you read the weight of those criteria differently, I regard B003 as a legitimate and cleanly attributed prize.

responses.point: Andersson moved to Calvo, Taylor and Woodford but argues that Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans is not merely derivative: identifying monetary shocks and estimating a medium-scale model is a different kind of contribution, and a citation limited to mechanisms and rules does not capture it.
responses.response: I agree, and it shaped my citation wording. The estimated-model tradition made the framework credible against data and usable in central banks, and a three-name award cannot reflect that. The honest position is that the citation recognises the conceptual foundations and is silent on the empirical implementation, which is a real omission and not a judgement that the empirical work is lesser. I would make the wording say so, and I would not defend the trio as the complete credit for the framework. Your point is also a reason I would accept Galí in place of Calvo only if the committee deliberately weights the citation toward the empirical and analytical framework. Otherwise I think the primitive-versus-development distinction favours Calvo.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B047 first for its cleaner attribution. He ranks B014 second because trios differ across colleagues, and he says Calvo's and Taylor's older contract-pricing and rule insights differ from the Woodford and Galí synthesis, so the committee must decide which it is crediting.
responses.response: The disagreement over trios shows that the attribution is contested, but I do not think it shows the contributions are indistinct. In the second round, every member who prefers B014 names the same trio, and members who differ on the third name say the choice is close. The citation does decide what is credited: the founding elements of the nominal-rigidity framework (Calvo, Taylor) together with the synthesis that made it a theory of policy (Woodford). It does not claim to credit Galí's development or the estimated tradition. I agree B047's two-name attribution is cleaner and that Melitz is unambiguous. I keep it as an alternative. I still rank it below B014 for two reasons: the Krugman (2008) overlap in subject, and the priority claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not credited on the entry. I would not count the absence of a trade prize since 2008 as merit, and I agree with your position on that.

responses.point: Hassler, who chairs, supports B014 and reads the post-2008 and post-2021 episodes as extension of the framework. He invited members who read them the other way to name the observation that would settle it. He accepts a Galí swap if the citation is weighted toward the empirical framework.
responses.response: I read the evidence as you do, but I would state what would change my view. If the pricing-friction and policy-rule components themselves failed to account for the inflation dynamics, with the shock mix not the explanation, I would treat that as a maturity problem and not as an extension. I have not seen evidence of that in the materials, and I cannot verify the empirical literature here, so I hold this as a judgement and not a finding. I also note that you, Krusell, Boppart and Friberg are co-authors, and that you chair. I try to ground my agreement in the structure of the contributions and not in the number of colleagues who name the same trio. On the Galí swap, we agree that it is the natural alternative and that the choice turns on what the citation weights.

uncertainties: Whether the third name should be Calvo or Galí. That depends on whether the committee wants a citation weighted toward primitives or toward the empirical and analytical framework. I would not object strongly to the swap.

Whether any three-person citation can avoid implying a ranking against Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler. I think the cap leaves this unresolvable, and the most the wording can do is not claim their contributions.
How the post-2021 inflation and the heterogeneous-agent critique bear on maturity: as extension of the framework, or as grounds to wait.
Whether the committee will apply a consistent standard on prior-prize overlap across B003 (2022), B032 (2024), B047 (2008) and the 2005-2020 game-theory prizes.
I have not independently verified priority, attribution or citation claims from outside the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No change. Nothing in my profile links me to Calvo, Taylor or Woodford, and my frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on any shortlisted entry. My field, labour economics and crime, is closest to B046 and B045, which are not in my configuration. I dropped B046 from my alternatives to make room for B003 after the exchange, not because of a changed view of its merit. The B003 and B047 credited names have no apparent connection to me either. Some committee colleagues who support B014, including the chair, co-author with one another, and I note that I have no co-authorship or institutional tie to them. Conflicts are disclosed, not adjudicated.
